newsitem.title: USA: Notes suggest Clinton fund-raising calls.
newsitem.headline: Notes suggest Clinton fund-raising calls.

text.p: In the latest twist to the Democratic Party's fund-raising controversy, congressional investigators are looking at a White House aide's handwritten notes for evidence as to whether President Clinton made solicitation calls to donors from the White House.
"BC made 15 to 20 calls, raised 500K," aide David Strauss wrote in 1994, according to his notes described by government officials on Friday.

The notes were among documents recently turned over to the House Government Reform and Oversight Committee that is investigating political fund-raising practices, mostly by the Democrats, from last year.
Government officials said the document also refers to calls made by first lady Hillary Rodham Clinton and Vice President Al Gore.
In addition, a February 1996 memo from then-White House deputy chief of staff Harold Ickes gave Clinton the names of 10 major corporate donors that the president could call, officials said.
Investigators have attempted to find out if Clinton made fund-raising calls from the White House. Federal law forbids government officials from soliciting political donations on government property.
The White House says Clinton does not remember making such calls from the White House.

"The president has made hundreds of phone calls to supporters over the years," said White House special counsel Lanny Davis. "On occasion the DNC (Democratic National Committee) would ask the president to make calls or would send him call sheets. The president may well have offered to make calls as well."
Davis pointed out that Clinton has said he cannot say that "out of the hundreds and hundreds and maybe thousands of calls" he made to supporters that he never asked for financial support.
"He said that he cannot recall specifically asking contributions during these calls though he may well have," Davis said.
